quizzes.stem: Scenario: Egret Support's request holds fixed rules, a conversation history at priority 5 and marketing blurbs at priority 1. It exceeds its token budget by a small margin. What does the assembler do?

options.a: Truncates the end of the rules until the whole request fits within the budget
options.b: Drops the conversation history first, because it is the largest block of the three
options.c: Refuses the request at once, since it is over budget by any amount at all
options.d: Sheds the least important block first, stopping as soon as it fits

explanation.d: The lowest-priority dynamic block goes first, and the assembler climbs only while the request is still over.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The static modules are never dropped".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the assembler drops the lowest first", by priority and not by size.
explanation.c: Ruled out because refusal is for when "only static modules remain and they still exceed the budget, the assembler refuses the request".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Heron Retail has four teams that each write the support prompt by hand as one string, with a slightly different order, and the cache hit rate is low. Which change helps most?

options.a: A reminder in the team wiki that the policy text ought to come first in the prompt
options.b: A longer cache lifetime, so that the different strings are all kept for longer
options.c: A standard header that every team adds to the start of its own prompt
options.d: A single assembler that arranges named modules, with callers passing only values

explanation.d: One assembler fixes the order, so every team's prefix matches.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a reminder leaves the order to each caller, where "the assembler decides the order and callers cannot".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Two requests share a cache entry only when everything up to the breakpoint is identical", and a longer lifetime does not make the strings identical.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a header does not fix the order that follows it: "The order is the same every time" only when one assembler decides it.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Osprey Support needs ticket tagging answered within 800 ms. Candidates A and B are capable enough and fast enough, and B costs less per output token. Candidate C costs less still, but it takes 1,400 ms. Which candidate should the plan pick?

options.a: C, since the lowest price decides the matter once capability has been established
options.b: B, the lowest-priced of the ones that satisfy every requirement
options.c: A, since the dearer option is the safer one for a first release to customers
options.d: Whichever the team used last, because consistency across workloads outweighs the saving

explanation.b: Latency rules C out, and price ranks the models that remain.
explanation.a: Ruled out because C fails the limit, and price "can only rank models that are already right".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the rule is to choose "among the models whose tier is at least the workload's and whose latency is within the limit" and take the cheapest, with no bonus for the dearer one.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the choice is "a design choice per workload", not one habit applied to all.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Kestrel Labs needs a model for a task at tier 3 with a latency limit of 500 ms. The candidates are a tier 3 model at 2,500 ms and a tier 2 model at 300 ms. What should the plan record?

options.a: The tier 2 candidate, since it is the only one that stays within the limit
options.b: The tier 3 candidate, since capability matters more than speed in a first release to customers
options.c: That nothing qualifies, since neither option satisfies both requirements
options.d: The cheaper of the two candidates, so that the budget of the project is protected

explanation.c: No candidate meets both the tier and the latency, so the finding is a mismatch that someone must resolve by relaxing a requirement.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A model below the tier fails the task".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the limit is part of the requirement too, and the candidate would fall under "A model slower than the limit".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Price comes last because it is the only fact that cannot make a model wrong".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Plover Insurance's assembler receives a dynamic module with the placeholder {claim_id}, and the caller supplies no value for it. What should the assembler do?

options.a: Send the request, leaving the placeholder in its text
options.b: Refuse to build the request, naming the absent item
options.c: Send it, replacing the placeholder with an empty string
options.d: Fill the gap with a guess, drawn from the caller's previous call

explanation.b: A missing value is a defect in the caller, so the assembler refuses and names it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A request that goes out with `{customer}` in its text" is sent with a gap that nobody checks.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a blank is the same silent defect, and "A missing variable is an error".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a guess invents data nobody supplied, and a request with a gap "is a defect that no model will report".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Teal Logistics runs a ticket tagger that must answer within 300 ms at tier 1, and its prompt carries a long block of unchanging text. Which two decisions follow?

options.a: Take the largest model for safety, and place the long text last in the request
options.b: Take the cheapest model of any tier, and place the long text in the final message
options.c: Take the model that was used last time, and cache the whole request as one piece
options.d: Take the cheapest that is capable and quick enough, and put the bulky constant passage first

explanation.d: The model is chosen by tier and latency with price ranking the rest, and the stable text leads so that it can be cached.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the largest model is not needed when "the cheapest model that meets the first two is the right one for each workload", and the page says "static modules first, in the order given, then the dynamic ones".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A model below the tier fails the task", whatever its price.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Two requests share a cache entry only when everything up to the breakpoint is identical", so the whole request, which includes the changing part, cannot be cached as one piece.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Avocet Travel builds a request from four pieces: the house rules, the fare policy, the traveller's current question and the traveller's earlier chat. Which arrangement fits best?

options.a: All four as static modules, so that they are cached together
options.b: Rules and question as static modules, policy and chat as dynamic ones
options.c: Fixed guidance as static modules, per-visit text as dynamic ones
options.d: All four as dynamic modules, so that any piece is edited freely

explanation.c: The pieces that never change go first as static modules, and the per-request pieces follow as dynamic ones, so that the stable prefix can be cached.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A static module whose text holds a `{variable}` is refused", and the question changes on every request.
explanation.b: Ruled out because it puts the changing question among the static modules and the stable policy among the dynamic ones, against "static modules first, in the order given, then the dynamic ones".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the cache works on "the request from its start up to a marked breakpoint", so with no static modules there is nothing to cache.
